questions.prompt: Which statement gives the core rule for “Periodic work and task delays”?
options: Start with a simple `loop()`; add tasks only for independent work with distinct timing needs.
The scheduler runs tasks; `vTaskDelay` lets other work use the CPU.
Each task consumes stack; priority affects scheduler choices.
`vTaskDelayUntil` preserves the intended period, but long blocking work can still miss a deadline.
questions.answer: `vTaskDelayUntil` preserves the intended period, but long blocking work can still miss a deadline.
questions.explanation:
`vTaskDelayUntil` preserves the intended period, but long blocking work can still miss a deadline.
Why: `vTaskDelay` blocks a task for a number of ticks; `pdMS_TO_TICKS` converts milliseconds to ticks. For periodic sampling, `vTaskDelayUntil` schedules from the prior release time, avoiding cumulative work-time drift. Tick resolution and scheduling latency are not microsecond guarantees, so measure the actual interval.
